audit_result.proof_trace: `_verifyTransferSignature` (LegionPositionManager.sol:L161) hashes `(from, to, positionId, msg.sender, address(this), chainId)` — no nonce and no deadline. ERC721 ownership provides implicit one-time-use protection under normal flow, but the admin `transferInvestorPosition` (onlyLegion, no signature) can return a position to `from`, after which the original authorization signature is fully replayable with no expiry. Other functions in the same codebase (`LegionPreLiquidApprovedSale`, `LegionCapitalRaise`) use an explicit `s_usedSignatures` mapping for replay protection; this function lacks an equivalent.
audit_result.attack_scenario: Legion admin issues a transfer authorization for (Alice → Bob, positionId=5); after the transfer is consumed, admin calls `transferInvestorPosition(Bob, Alice, 5)` to return the position; `Caller1` then replays the original signature via `transferInvestorPositionWithAuthorization(Alice, Bob, 5, sig)`, which passes all checks and re-executes the transfer without a new authorization.

PROP-01b-partial-asm-002.assertion: forall authSig: authSig.params include (nonce OR deadline) preventing cross-context replay
